{{notability|Biographies|date=April 2013}}

'''Praful D. Bhavsar'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Felicitation of Prof. P.D. Bhavsar on his 97th Birthday, by Director SAC |url=https://www.sac.gov.in/SacSliderI_Repository/Vyom/English/777/Felicitation%20of%20Prof.%20P.D.%20Bhavsar_17-8-2022.pdf |website=sac.gov.in |publisher=Space Applications Centre |access-date=24 September 2022}}</ref> (17 August 1926 – 30 September 2023) was an Indian space scientist who held several major positions in the Indian Space program including the Project Scientist for the first rocket launch into space from Indian soil on 21 November 1963. In 1986, he retired from the position of Director, [[Space Applications Centre]] of the [[Indian Space Research Organization]] (ISRO)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |title=Space Applications Centre |website=www.sac.gov.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093332/http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |archive-date=2015-09-24}} </ref>
and the Director, Indian Remote Sensing Satellite Utilization Program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/319625/first-remote-sensing-satellite-programme.html|title=First remote sensing satellite programme team felicitated|work=Deccan Herald|accessdate=19 September 2014|date=2013-03-17}}</ref>

Bhavsar was born on 17 August 1926,<ref>{{cite news |title=Felicitation of Prof. P.D. Bhavsar on his 97th Birthday, by Director SAC |url=https://www.sac.gov.in/SacSliderI_Repository/Vyom/English/777/Felicitation%20of%20Prof.%20P.D.%20Bhavsar_17-8-2022.pdf |access-date=7 December 2022 |publisher=sac.gov.in |date=17 August 2022}}</ref> and received his Doctorate in Physics from [[Gujarat University]] in 1958 for his research in [[Cosmic Rays]] at the [[Physical Research Laboratory]] under the guidance of [[Vikram Sarabhai]].  In the same year he moved to the [[University of Minnesota]] as a research fellow in the laboratory of Professor [[John R. Winckler]] to study high altitude Cosmic Rays using balloons.  Whilst at Minnesota, Bhavsar also collaborated with Professor [[Jacques Blamont]] who would later play a key role in India's first rocket launch.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diploweb.com/_Jacques-BLAMONT_.html|title=Jacques BLAMONT|accessdate=29 August 2015}}</ref>

The Scientific and Technical Sub-committee of the [[United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space]] (COSPAR) was established in 1958. One of its objectives was to foster international scientific collaboration. In 1962 Indian National Committee for Space Research [[INCOSPAR]] was established by the Indian government under the chairmanship of Dr [[Vikram Sarabhai]]. One of its first projects was the establishment of the [[Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station]] (TERLS) in the district of Trivandrum on the southern tip of India very close to [[Magnetic dip|Earth's magnetic equator]].

Bhavsar was a student<ref>Vikram Sarabhai: A Life by Amrita Shah, 2007, Penguin Viking {{ISBN|0-670-99951-2}} [P97]</ref> of Dr.[[Vikram Sarabhai]], and at his request returned to India and joined a team of scientists as the project scientist that launched India's first rocket from the [[Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station]] (TERLS). The two stage Nike-Apache [[sounding rocket]] came from the USA and the French payload that left a vertical trail of sodium vapour in the upper atmosphere from a 100 to 120&nbsp;km altitude. The primary purpose of this flight was to measure atmospheric winds, temperature, diffusion and turbulence by photographing the trail of the ejected sodium.

Bhavsar held many prestigious positions over the years, including: Scientific Co-ordinator, [[ISRO]] (1967–1975); Member-Secretary<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |title=Space Applications Centre |website=www.sac.gov.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093332/http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |archive-date=2015-09-24}} </ref>[[INCOSPAR]] (1970–1981); Chairman – Remote Sensing Area, [[Space Applications Center]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |title=Space Applications Centre |website=www.sac.gov.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093332/http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |archive-date=2015-09-24}} </ref> (1976–1984); Director, Indian Remote Sensing Satellite Utilization Programme (1981–1986);<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |title=Space Applications Centre |website=www.sac.gov.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093332/http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |archive-date=2015-09-24}} </ref> and Director, [[Space Applications Center]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |title=Space Applications Centre |website=www.sac.gov.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093332/http://www.sac.gov.in/SACSITE/asac-leaders-pdbhavsar.html |archive-date=2015-09-24}} </ref> [[ISRO]] (1985–1986).
 
In 1999 Bhavsar was awarded the Aryabhata Award<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asindia.org/bhavsar.aspx|title=Astronautical Society of India - ASIndia.org|accessdate=19 September 2014}}</ref> in recognition of his lifetime achievement in the area of [[Astronautics]] by the Astronautical Society of India.

Praful Bhavsar died on 30 September 2023, at the age of 97.<ref>{{cite news |title=India’s rocket hero Prof Praful Bhavsar no more |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/indias-rocket-hero-prof-praful-bhavsar-no-more/articleshow/104078491.cms?from=mdr |access-date=5 October 2023 |publisher=The Times of India |date=1 October 2023}}</ref>
